newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka opposition complains of attacks ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka opposition complains of attacks ahead of poll.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) on Wednesday accused the government and police of turning a blind eye to large scale attacks against its candidates before next month's key local elections.
"UNP candidates are being attacked and threatened but the police are not taking any action," former prime minister and UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe told a news conference.
"This local authority election is the most violent local election in our history," he said.

More than 18,000 candidates from 12 political parties, including the ruling People's Alliance (PA), the UNP and 132 independent groups, will take part in the polls for 238 local government bodies, the Elections Department has said.
It will be the PA government's first popularity test since winning power in 1994.

Wickremesinghe said that UNP members had made 162 complaints of violence and intimidation to police up to Tuesday. At the same time, he also acknowledged that there were complaints of violence against UNP members.

"We want the police to inquire into all complaints," Wickremasinghe said. "Our grievance is that the police are not being allowed to act. Any UNP (member) found guilty of violence will be expelled from the party."
He said the UNP was prepared to cooperate with the government in its effort to recover thousands of firearms issued to members of political parties for self-defence.
Police on Wednesday declined to comment on Wickremasinghe's statements and government officials were not immediately available.
Police have launched a nationwide crackdown on unlicensed guns to curb political violence before the polls, already marred by the killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker.

Police said 17 suspects are in custody for the killing earlier this month of MP Nalanda Ellawala in Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo. Among the suspects were UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former UNP mayor.
Both have been suspended from the party, Wickremesinghe said.
Ellawala's death sparked riots in the southern gem mining town of Ratnapura and angry ruling party supporters torched buildings belonging to rival UNP supporters.
